name: Low-dose doxepin (Silenor)

lead: Low-dose doxepin (Silenor) is a prescription sleep medicine approved in 2010 for staying asleep. It is a tricyclic antidepressant sold at much lower strengths for this purpose.
No studies link it to appearance outcomes.

paras: At low strengths it mainly blocks histamine H1 receptors, producing sedation; at antidepressant strengths reuptake inhibition predominates.
Reported effects include sedation, dry mouth, constipation and blood pressure drops on standing. It is contraindicated with MAO inhibitors and is Rx-only.

lead: Doxepin is a tricyclic compound first approved by the US FDA in 1969 as an antidepressant under the brand name Sinequan. A low-dose oral tablet, Silenor, was approved in 2010 for insomnia characterised by difficulty staying asleep [1]. A 5% topical cream is approved for itching in atopic dermatitis or lichen simplex chronicus [1].

At the low strengths sold for insomnia, doxepin's sedating effect is attributed mainly to histamine H1 receptor antagonism [1][2]. No study has examined it for appearance outcomes, and no looksmaxxing community material was identified.
The American Academy of Sleep Medicine 2017 guideline includes low-dose doxepin among its recommendations for sleep maintenance insomnia [3].
infobox: Tricyclic; H1 antagonist at low doses

paras: Silenor is indicated for sleep maintenance insomnia in adults [1][3]. Higher-strength doxepin is used for depression and anxiety, where reuptake inhibition of serotonin and noradrenaline is considered to predominate [1]. Trials have also examined doxepin for urticaria and for uraemic itch [4][5].

Reported effects include sedation, dry mouth, constipation and low blood pressure on standing; contraindications include use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors and glaucoma or urinary retention conditions [1]. A study of anticholinergic activity in medications used by older adults is a source for its anticholinergic burden [6]. Genotype guidelines address CYP2D6 and CYP2C19 effects on tricyclic dosing [7].
A 2011 Nature paper reported the structure of the human histamine H1 receptor bound to doxepin, which underpins its description as a potent H1 antagonist [2].

Phase 2 trial NCT00755495 enrolled 472 people with chronic insomnia to compare ramelteon and doxepin [8]. The AASM guideline reviewed trials of low-dose doxepin in sleep maintenance [3]. Other registered trials studied doxepin for uraemic pruritus and urticaria [4][5]. No studies were found on doxepin for appearance outcomes.

timeline.event: Approved by the US FDA for depression and anxiety [1].
